value_stream.name: Merchandise Financial Planning, Open-to-Buy & Margin Management

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, Supply Planning (links to VS-02.1), Allocation (links to VS-55)

workflows.name: Ending Stock & Weeks-of-Supply (WOS) Target Planning by Category

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Merchandise Planner set EOM stock targets and weeks-of-supply" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconcile to receipt plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor actual WOS weekly" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: OTB discipline (W3283); operational: safety-stock policy and reforecast (W3288)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-stock risk**: Excess WOS ties up working capital and ages inventory (W3294); mitigated by OTB discipline (W3283)
- **Stockout risk**: Insufficient WOS on A-items loses sales; mitigated by safety-stock policy and reforecast (W3288)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise planning; demand planning (links to VS-02.1); allocation (links to VS-55); BI (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner set EOM stock targets and weeks-of-supply (WOS) by category using forward demand (links to VS-02.1), lead time (domestic 7–21d / import 45–90d per VS-02.2), safety-stock policy (A/B/C per profile §6.6), and seasonality
Category Managers confirm category WOS supports service-level targets and key-item availability; reconcile to receipt plan (W3284) and store-cluster needs (W3302)
Merchandise Planner publish WOS/EOM targets to supply planning and allocation; monitor actual WOS weekly (W3288) and flag over/under-stock

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Finance (links to VS-17.1)

workflows.name: Inventory Turn & GMROI Target Setting & Performance Tracking

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Merchandise Planner set inventory-turn targets" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track actual turn and GMROI monthly by category, isolate drivers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "review category turn/GMROI with Category Managers quarterly" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: GMROI discipline and space reallocation; operational: maintained-margin modeling (W3286)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capital-trap risk**: Capital trapped in low-turn categories erodes ROIC; mitigated by GMROI discipline and space reallocation
- **Margin-vs-turn trade-off risk**: Chasing turn via markdown erodes margin; mitigated by maintained-margin modeling (W3286)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise planning; GL/inventory valuation (links to VS-17.1); BI (links to VS-28.1); space analytics (links to VS-55.3)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner set inventory-turn targets (corporate 6–8x per profile §12.3) and GMROI (gross-margin return on inventory investment) targets by category, benchmarking to category role (destination vs routine vs seasonal)

Merchandise Planner/Finance track actual turn and GMROI monthly by category, isolate drivers (sales velocity, stock level, margin), and flag underperformers for action (markdown W3285, cancel W3284, transfer links to VS-05.2)

VP Merchandising review category turn/GMROI with Category Managers quarterly; reallocate OTB and space (links to VS-55.3) toward higher-productivity categories and exit chronic underperformers (W3293)

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Supply Planning (links to VS-02.1), DC ops (links to VS-04), Buyers (links to VS-03)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "Merchandise Planner/Supply Planning convert stock-to-sales targets into a receipt" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor actual stock-to-sales weekly" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: flow planning and reforecast; operational: smoothing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Flow-mismatch risk**: Receipt timing off vs demand creates stockouts or overstock; mitigated by flow planning and reforecast
- **Inbound-congestion risk**: Receipt peaks overwhelm DC inbound (links to VS-04.1); mitigated by smoothing
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise planning; demand/supply planning (links to VS-02.1); DC capacity (links to VS-04.3)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner set monthly stock-to-sales ratio targets by category (beginning stock as a multiple of the month's planned sales) to ensure flow supports demand without overstock

Merchandise Planner/Supply Planning convert stock-to-sales targets into a receipt flow plan timed to lead times (domestic/import) and DC capacity (links to VS-04.3); smooth receipts to avoid inbound peaks
Merchandise Planner monitor actual stock-to-sales weekly (W3288) and adjust flow (chase/cancel/transfer) to maintain target

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Allocation (links to VS-55), New-Store team (links to VS-37), Buyers (links to VS-03), Finance (links to VS-40)
fields.Volume: Per new store (~35,000 SKU initial stock)

workflows.name: New-Store Inventory Investment Planning & Pre-Open Stock Build

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow orchestration of "coordinate DC staging" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track the new-store inventory investment" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: cluster-based sizing and post-open stabilization (links to VS-37); operational: capex planning (links to VS-40)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under/over-stock risk**: Initial stock mismatch causes early stockouts or aged inventory; mitigated by cluster-based sizing and post-open stabilization (links to VS-37.3)
- **Capital-timing risk**: Initial stock build ties up working capital before revenue; mitigated by capex planning (links to VS-40)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise/allocation planning (links to VS-55); store opening (links to VS-37); capex (links to VS-40); DC staging (links to VS-04)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/Allocation develop the new-store initial stock (HOT / hand-over stock) plan by department/category based on store format (8,000–15,000 sqm), cluster, and localization (links to VS-55.3 W2186); size the inventory investment and OTB impact

Buyers/Supply Planning procure initial stock to land pre-opening per the store-opening plan (links to VS-37.1/VS-37.2); coordinate DC staging (links to VS-04) and phased fill to avoid single-day inbound overload
Finance/Merchandise Planner capitalize and track the new-store inventory investment (links to VS-40 capex), confirm OTB absorption, and reconcile post-opening to plan (links to VS-37.3 stabilization)

fields.Participants: Category Manager, Merchandise Planner, Allocation, Pricing (links to VS-01.2/VS-64), Reverse Logistics (links to VS-32/VS-05.3)
fields.Trigger: SKU/category exit decision (links to VS-01.1 lifecycle); vendor exit; private-label refresh (links to VS-41)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify discontinuing SKUs/categories, stop replenishment" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate channel clearance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconcile exit inventory to zero on-hand, capture realized margin/loss vs plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: structured clearance and disposition; operational: early exit decisioning and markdown budget discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-inventory risk**: Poor exit planning leaves dead stock and write-offs (W3294); mitigated by structured clearance and disposition
- **Margin-loss risk**: Forced liquidation erodes margin; mitigated by early exit decisioning and markdown budget discipline
System Touchpoints: - Lifecycle/discontinuation (links to VS-01.1); clearance (links to VS-64); reverse logistics (links to VS-32/VS-05.3); master data (links to VS-29); GL (links to VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Category Manager plan the exit: identify discontinuing SKUs/categories, stop replenishment (cancel open PO per VS-03.2), set sell-through timeline, and choose disposition (markdown to clear, vendor return per VS-32.2, transfer per VS-05.2, liquidation per VS-05.3)

Pricing/Category Manager execute clearance pricing (links to VS-64.2 markdown clearance) within markdown budget (W3285); coordinate channel clearance (links to VS-65/VS-95 marketplace) and store execution
Merchandise Planner reconcile exit inventory to zero on-hand, capture realized margin/loss vs plan (W3286), retire the SKU master (links to VS-29), and report exit performance

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, Finance (links to VS-17.1), Internal Audit (links to VS-21.1)
fields.Trigger: Monthly aging review; period-end close (links to VS-17.1)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "Merchandise Planner run monthly inventory aging" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track reserve roll-forward, provision accuracy, and aged-inventory reduction…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: PFRS discipline and aging review; operational: monthly cadence and OTB discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-provision risk**: Inadequate reserve overstates inventory/assets; mitigated by PFRS discipline and aging review
- **Aged-buildup risk**: Slow reaction to aging compounds write-offs; mitigated by monthly cadence and OTB discipline
System Touchpoints: - Inventory aging/analytics; GL provisioning (links to VS-17.1); disposition (links to VS-05.3/VS-32/VS-64); audit (links to VS-21.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner run monthly inventory aging (e.g., 90/180/365 days) and slow-mover report (turn below threshold) by category/store; identify aged stock and root cause (overbuy, demand miss, seasonality)

Category Manager/Merchandise Planner decide action (markdown W3285, transfer per VS-05.2, vendor return per VS-32.2, clearance links to VS-64, write-off); Finance assess and book lower-of-cost-or-net-realizable-value provision per PFRS (links to VS-17.1)
Merchandise Planner/Finance track reserve roll-forward, provision accuracy, and aged-inventory reduction trend; report to VP Merchandising and audit (links to VS-21.1)

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Import/Buyers (links to VS-02.2/VS-03), Customs (links to VS-87), Treasury (links to VS-18.3), Finance (links to VS-17.1)
fields.Trigger: Sourcing strategy; FX movement (links to VS-18.3); cost change

workflows.name: Import vs Domestic Inventory Investment & Landed-Cost Margin Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "Import model landed cost for import SKUs" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track actual landed-cost margin vs plan, isolate duty/FX/freight variance, and…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: landed-cost modeling and FTA optimization (links to VS-87); operational: FX hedging (links to VS-18)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Landed-cost-blindness risk**: Import margin eroded by hidden duty/freight; mitigated by landed-cost modeling and FTA optimization (links to VS-87.2)
- **FX-exposure risk**: PHP depreciation raises import cost; mitigated by FX hedging (links to VS-18.3) and sourcing diversification
System Touchpoints: - Landed-cost module; import/customs (links to VS-02.2/VS-87); FX (links to VS-18.3); GL (links to VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/Import model landed cost for import SKUs (product cost + freight + duty/tariff per VS-87 + brokerage + insurance per VS-02.2 W191) vs domestic cost; compute margin under each sourcing option and FX scenario (links to VS-18.3)

Category Managers decide import-vs-domestic mix per SKU/category considering landed-cost margin, lead time (45–90d import), quality (links to VS-31), MOQ, and duty-deferral/bonded options (links to VS-87.2/VS-02.2 W284); commit OTB accordingly (W3284)
Finance/Merchandise Planner track actual landed-cost margin vs plan, isolate duty/FX/freight variance, and feed to margin plan (W3286) and close (links to VS-17.1)

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Treasury (links to VS-18.1), VP Merchandising, CFO
fields.Trigger: Annual plan; strategic review; cash/working-capital constraint (links to VS-18.1)

workflows.name: Inventory Investment Scenario Modeling & Working-Capital Constraint

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-forecast of "Treasury/CFO set the working-capital/cash constraint" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "VP Merchandising/CFO select the plan scenario, communicate OTB and" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-533 (ensure controlled execution — Inventory Investment, Turn & Productivity Planning (PA-101.2).)
- operational: working-capital-constrained scenario; operational: scenario trade-off analysis
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-investment risk**: Inventory grows faster than cash/turn supports; mitigated by working-capital-constrained scenario
- **Under-investment risk**: Over-tight constraint starves growth and loses sales; mitigated by scenario trade-off analysis
System Touchpoints: - Scenario/planning model; cash forecasting (links to VS-18.1); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); OTB (W3283)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/FP&A model inventory-investment scenarios (growth vs conservative vs working-capital-constrained) across the plan: project EOM inventory $, OTB, cash tied up, turn, and margin under each

Treasury/CFO set the working-capital/cash constraint (links to VS-18.1 cash forecast); Merchandise Planner right-size OTB and receipt flow (W3284) to fit the cash envelope without breaching service-level targets

VP Merchandising/CFO select the plan scenario, communicate OTB and inventory-investment limits to Buyers/Planners, and monitor adherence via weekly P&A (W3288) and monthly cash review (links to VS-18.1)
